## Problem

## Problem

Design and implement a custom `Vector` class in C++ that behaves as a dynamic array. Leverage modern C++ techniques—particularly metaprogramming and the RAII idiom—to achieve both safety and efficiency. The class must internally handle its own memory management without relying on standard library containers.

The `Vector` must support:
- Adding elements at the end
- Deleting elements
- Accessing elements through indexing

Strive to incorporate as many contemporary C++ features as you can throughout the implementation.

## Constraints

- The implementation must manage all allocated memory automatically, freeing resources when no longer needed and avoiding leaks.
- Resizing (when adding beyond capacity) should preserve existing elements.
- Index-based access should be efficient.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Use RAII to manage a raw pointer to a dynamically allocated array, with copy constructor and assignment operator to handle deep copies.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Leverage template metaprogramming to support any data type and to enable compile-time optimizations like type traits.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The key trade-off is between performance (e.g., using memcpy for POD types) and safety (e.g., proper exception handling during reallocation).

</details>
